quarterly_data.signal: Q2 FY2026 results for the quarter ended December 31, 2025 (CFO): record revenue of $12.7 billion, up 123% year-over-year and up 153% quarter-over-quarter, against guidance of $10 billion to $11 billion. Q2 revenue included approximately $1.5 billion of Q1 shipments delayed by customer readiness. Growth came from the rapid ramp and deployment of Rack Scale AI solutions, and AI GPU platforms were over 90% of Q2 revenue. Non-GAAP gross margin was 6.4% (9.5% in Q1) and non-GAAP operating margin was 4.5% (5.4% in Q1), with non-GAAP operating expenses at 1.9% of revenue. Non-GAAP diluted EPS was $0.69 against guidance of $0.46 to $0.54 (GAAP EPS $0.60).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $12.7 billion (+123% YoY, +153% QoQ; incl. approximately $1.5 billion delayed Q1 shipments); AI GPU platforms over 90% of revenue; non-GAAP gross margin 6.4%; non-GAAP EPS $0.69

quarterly_data.signal: Why gross margin fell (CEO/CFO): customer and product mix, with the mix shifting further toward large model builders that have pricing leverage. Other factors were higher freight, production and expedite costs 'as we began to ship new platforms on a large scale', plus tariffs. CEO on the new rack platform: 'the GP300 was a little bit new to us. So a lot of expedite transportation cost. And now, I mean, product is getting mature. So those expedite transportation costs will be dramatically reduced and tariff impact also improving.' He expects the customer mix to improve, gross margin to rise quarter after quarter, and said 'the gross margin -- net margin ratio, we are expecting to grow to a double digit as soon as possible'. The CFO did not size the individual cost items. Q3 gross margin is guided up 30 basis points from Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 non-GAAP gross margin 6.4% (vs 9.5% in Q1); Q3 gross margin guided up 30 basis points

quarterly_data.signal: Outlook (CEO/CFO): Q3 FY2026 net sales of at least $12.3 billion, GAAP diluted EPS of at least $0.52 and non-GAAP diluted EPS of at least $0.60, with Q3 capital expenditures of $70 million to $90 million. Full fiscal year 2026 net sales are guided to at least $40 billion. The CEO said he could 'up our full year revenue guidance back to at least $40 billion' because of the broad customer back order forecast and commitments, and called 'minimum $40 billion' 'a relatively conservative number'. He described demand for AI and IT infrastructure as 'unprecedentedly strong', and the CFO said orders remain strong from global large data center and enterprise customers. CEO aspiration: 'Very soon, I hope I can say we have more than $50 billion or $60 billion revenue'.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 FY2026 net sales at least $12.3 billion; non-GAAP EPS at least $0.60; FY2026 net sales at least $40 billion; Q3 capex $70 million to $90 million

quarterly_data.signal: Customer concentration and mix (CFO): one large data center customer (not named) was approximately 63% of total Q2 revenue. OEM appliance and large data center revenue was $10.7 billion, approximately 84% of revenue versus 68% last quarter (up 151% YoY and 210% QoQ). By geography the U.S. was 86% of Q2 revenue (U.S. revenue up 184% YoY), Asia 9%, Europe 3% and the rest of the world 2%. Asked whether the 63% customer had been a 10% customer before, the CFO said only that Super Micro 'does most of its business with repeat customers' and has 'added a lot of new logos', and referred to the 10-K and 10-Qs. The CEO said the customer base now has 'many more large-scale customers' and is becoming more diversified, although customers sometimes pull in or push out their schedules.
quarterly_data.figure: one customer approximately 63% of total revenue; OEM appliance and large data center $10.7 billion (approximately 84% of revenue); U.S. 86% of revenue

quarterly_data.signal: Working capital funds the order ramp (CFO): Q2 closing inventory was $10.6 billion, up from $5.7 billion in Q1, 'as we prepared for continuing strength in Q3 shipments'. The cash conversion cycle improved from 123 days to 54 days. Operating cash use was $24 million, capex $21 million and free cash flow negative $45 million. Cash was $4.1 billion against $4.9 billion of bank and convertible note debt, for net debt of $787 million. New funding: a $2 billion secured revolving credit facility in the U.S., an approximately $1.8 billion secured Taiwan revolving debt facility closed in January, and an accounts receivable factoring facility (unused in the December quarter, used since), giving 'access to over $5 billion of additional capital'. The CFO tied the rise in receivables and inventory to having 'well in excess of $13 billion of orders' for delivery, as he had said the previous quarter.
quarterly_data.figure: inventory $10.6 billion (from $5.7 billion); well in excess of $13 billion of orders; access to over $5 billion of additional capital; net debt $787 million

players.product: GPU server systems and NVL rack integration

quarterly_data.signal: Component shortage (CEO): near-term margin pressure includes 'key component shortage like memory and storage shortage', and Q2 gross margin was hit by the ongoing component shortage and volatile component pricing. The CEO said the key component shortage exists 'because the demand is getting so strong, not because of production capacity is reduced', and that the cost impact 'won't hurt us too much'. The full-year guide of at least $40 billion already assumes component prices keep rising and is conservative for that reason: 'If the cost -- if the shortage situation improve quickly, for sure, our [indiscernible] revenue will be more than that.'
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 guide of at least $40 billion already assumes rising component prices

quarterly_data.signal: DCBBS (Data Center Building Block Solutions) economics and roadmap (CEO): DCBBS accounted for 4% of profit in the first half of fiscal 2026. Those were its first two quarters, since the line was officially introduced about 6 months ago. Revenue is still relatively small, but the margin is much better, 'for sure, more than 20%'. DCBBS profit should contribute meaningfully in 2H FY2026 and reach 'at least double-digit contribution by end of calendar 2026'. In about a year the line grew to more than 10 key subsystems: CDU, heat exchanger, chilled doors, power shelves, battery backup, water tower, dry-towers, high-speed switching, data center management software and service. Another 3 to 5 items are planned in the next few months or quarters, and the CEO said the line is expanding into new categories such as transformers, next-generation power generators, energy backup devices and grid power replacement. It is sold globally as a one-stop shop to large, mid-size and small data center builders to shorten time-to-deployment and time-to-online and to reduce power and water consumption.
quarterly_data.figure: DCBBS 4% of profit in 1H FY2026; at least double-digit profit contribution by end of calendar 2026; margin more than 20%; more than 10 key subsystems, another 3 to 5 items planned

quarterly_data.signal: Manufacturing footprint and cost structure (CEO): the Silicon Valley facility remains the cornerstone of U.S. operations. New production sites in Taiwan, Malaysia, the Netherlands and the Middle East are ramping to add capacity, serve regional AI requirements and optimize overall cost structure, and the CEO listed international facility expansion as a near-term margin headwind. Design-for-manufacturing work (more modularized subsystems, expanded automation across facilities) is raising yield and bringing new platforms to volume production faster.

Vera Rubin preparation (CEO): Supermicro is 'also preparing for upcoming NVIDIA, Vera Rubin and AMD Helios solutions for the second half this year'. Asked whether orders had started for second-half delivery, he said 'we have a lot of highly interested customers, some already engaged' and that 'today, we already have some good commitment from customers'. Timing 'depends on our partner, depends on when their Vera Rubin or AMD solution will be ready'. On differentiation in the Vera Rubin cycle, he said Supermicro optimizes the whole DCBBS for customers based on NVIDIA's solution (energy consumption, energy backup and, 'maybe too early to say', grid power replacement). Speaking generally about time-to-market, he expects to keep bringing total solutions to market ahead of others, 'if not 6 months earlier, at least 3 months or 4 months earlier'.
quarterly_data.figure: Vera Rubin solutions targeted for the second half this year; time-to-market lead of 'if not 6 months earlier, at least 3 months or 4 months earlier'

quarterly_data.signal: Enterprise diversification (CEO/CFO): the enterprise channel segment was $2 billion in Q2, about 16% of revenue versus 31% in the prior quarter (up 42% YoY and 29% QoQ). Supermicro is sharpening its focus on traditional enterprise, cloud and edge IoT customers to diversify revenue toward higher margins. It introduced X14 and H14 solutions: preconfigured systems that ship directly from the factory, are optimized for specific AI, cloud, storage and telco edge workloads, and are 'ready to power immediately' for enterprise customers, channel partners and SMB end users. The CEO said the company is 'very aggressively growing enterprise midsized' accounts while still pursuing large accounts.
quarterly_data.figure: enterprise channel revenue $2 billion (about 16% of revenue vs 31% prior quarter; up 42% YoY)
